# Copilot Instructions

## Repository purpose

This repository defines a VS Code Copilot custom agent that will scaffold a
cross-platform Rust/Cargo Hello World project and its GitHub Actions CI. The
customization layer is the current source of truth: the generated Rust source,
Cargo files, CI scripts, and workflow are produced later by the agent.

The primary entry point is the `build-engineer` custom agent. Its orchestration
command is `/init`.

At the current repository state, the implementation layer (`src/`, `tests/`,
`Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `ci.sh`, `ci.bat`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and
`.gitignore`) has not yet been generated. Do not treat missing implementation
files as an instruction to invent or silently create them outside the
documented `/init` workflow.

## Build, test, and validation commands

The implementation files are generated by the prompts, so run these commands
after `/create-build` has produced the Cargo project:

```text
cargo build
cargo build --release
cargo test
cargo test --release
```

To run only the integration test:

```text
cargo test --test test_basic
```

To run only the named test:

```text
cargo test basic_addition
```

The project-specific CI scripts are the canonical cross-platform build entry
points after they exist:

```text
# Linux/macOS
./ci.sh

# Windows
ci.bat
```

`ci.sh` must run release build, release tests, create `dist/`, and copy the
release executable. `ci.bat` performs the equivalent Windows operations and
checks `%errorlevel%` after each command.

Validate the GitHub Actions workflow with either command when the workflow has
been generated:

```text
python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))"
actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

The repository's read-only validation command is `/check`. It must report
`Статус: PASSED` before the overall initialization is considered successful.
Until `/init` has generated the implementation layer and Rust is installed,
Cargo and CI commands cannot pass; report their exact failure instead of
claiming success.

## High-level architecture

The workflow is deliberately split into three customization primitives:

1. `.github/agents/build-engineer.agent.md` defines the build-engineer role,
   allowed tools, skills, commands, safety rules, and completion criteria.
2. `.github/skills/` contains focused procedures:
   - `project-scaffold` creates `src/lib.rs`, `src/main.rs`, and the initial
     project structure for `language=Rust`, `project_name=hello`;
   - `build-and-test` maps those sources into `Cargo.toml`, adds
     `tests/test_basic.rs`, generates `Cargo.lock`, and creates `ci.sh` and
     `ci.bat`;
   - `github-actions` creates the workflow that runs the platform-specific CI
     script and uploads `dist/`.
3. `.github/prompts/` exposes the procedures as user-facing commands. `/init`
   runs `/git-init`, `/create-project`, `/create-build`, `/create-actions`, and
   `/check` in that exact order.

The data flow is:

```text
project_name=hello -> src/ -> Cargo.toml -> ci.sh/ci.bat -> ci.yml
```

The workflow intentionally keeps Rust commands in `ci.sh` and `ci.bat`.
`ci.yml` should only select the runner, check out the repository, invoke the
appropriate script, and upload `dist/`.

## Repository-specific conventions

- Instructions and documentation are written in Ukrainian. File names,
  command names, Rust identifiers, and Cargo/action identifiers remain in
  English.
- Treat the customization files as an idempotent pipeline. Inspect an existing
  file before changing it; do not duplicate sections, tests, commands, or
  workflow steps.
- Do not overwrite a conflicting existing file automatically. Report the
  difference and stop for that file.
- `/check` is read-only. It may allow Cargo to create temporary `target/`
  artifacts, but it must not repair files, the Git index, or configuration.
- `/init` is fail-fast: after any failed step, stop and report the step,
  cause, and corrective action. Never report success without the final
  `check` status.
- The expected Rust library is `hello_lib::add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32`; the
  integration test is named `basic_addition`.
- The expected binary is `hello`. Unix uses
  `target/release/hello`; Windows uses `target\release\hello.exe`. The CI
  scripts copy the platform-specific executable into `dist/`.
- The Actions matrix must use `ubuntu-latest`, `windows-latest`, and
  `macos-latest` with `fail-fast: false`. Unix invokes `./ci.sh` with Bash;
  Windows invokes `ci.bat` with `cmd`.
- Keep generated build output out of version control. The required ignored
  entries are `target/`, `build/`, and `dist/`; the repository setup also
  ignores `out/`, `.vs/`, `.env`, `*.pem`, and `*.key`.
- Do not create or expose secrets, tokens, passwords, or private keys.
- Do not delete files, force-push, rewrite history, or change branch
  protection.

## Source of truth

When behavior is unclear, consult the relevant file rather than duplicating
rules:

- Agent behavior: `.github/agents/build-engineer.agent.md`
- Scaffold procedure: `.github/skills/project-scaffold/SKILL.md`
- Build and test procedure: `.github/skills/build-and-test/SKILL.md`
- Actions procedure: `.github/skills/github-actions/SKILL.md`
- Command behavior: `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`
- User workflow and command list: `README.md`
- Component relationships and data flow: `docs/architecture.md`
